geographic_notes.text: The September 2025 BTR describes historical salinity intrusion and damage to Rosetta's coastal agriculture and freshwater. Its salinity unit and underlying studies need confirmation before the percentage is reused.

The 2025 BTR reports an irrigation-modernization programme covering a stated four-million-feddan ambition, with an expected 20% water-efficiency gain. These are reported implementation scope and targets, not independently verified achieved savings.

Source dated not stated reports: The ministry describes GCF-backed nature-based protection for 69 km across Kafr El-Sheikh, Beheira, Port Said, Dakahlia and New Damietta, alongside a planned integrated-management strategy for 1,200 km of Mediterranean coast.

Source dated not stated reports: The coastal project also proposes small livelihood pilots with civil-society and research partners, including greenhouses and fishing-net support for local residents and small farmers.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 9 of 9 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
Searches found no direct country-specific evidence linking climate hazards to armed conflict or showing conflict itself blocking climate adaptation.
Some BTR adaptation figures are planned targets or government-reported implementation without an independent outcome assessment; the 2022 CCDR remains a dated executive-summary baseline.
Egypt's latest NDC/BTR update after the 2025 BTR was not verified in this extraction.
No supported climate-to-violence or reverse insecurity-to-adaptation chain is assembled. Nile external water dependence is not itself evidence of interstate conflict.
